item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00161","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C11","C16","C04"],"selected_candidate_label":"C11","confidence":0.78,"relationship_type":"structural_functional_template","rationale":"C11 plausibly supplied a material structural template for the child. Both are Eisenhower veto memoranda concerning special benefits for a limited class of government employees. Each first explains the proposed benefit and its financing, then rejects extending a preferential arrangement to another employee group, acknowledges that the underlying problem or objective is legitimate, advocates a coordinated system-wide solution, and closes by promising further study or recommendations to Congress. C16 closely shares the argument that a problem affecting one employee group should be addressed through general legislation, while C04 shares the objections to shifting private or nonfederal costs to the United States and creating an undesirable precedent. Neither matches the child's full argumentative sequence as closely as C11.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"The bill is not approved because it would (1) make improper use of Federal funds ... (2) result in an unsound shifting of fiscal responsibility ... (3) set an undesirable precedent, and (4) constitute an unsound approach to a desirable goal of increased employee mobility.","parent_excerpt":"The claims of the inspectional employees for equal treatment with other inspectional groups have much merit, but equality of treatment for all inspectional employees is not brought about by this bill. Furthermore, the special pay features of the bill depart from principles of overtime and premium pay ...","explanation":"Both frame a legitimate employee-policy objective as pursued through an unsound, preferential, and fiscally problematic mechanism."},{"child_excerpt":"This unsound fiscal policy could become an even more serious matter if the program were to be extended to all employee groups having similar claims.","parent_excerpt":"I do not believe extending their use to other groups of Federal employees would be good management. Legislation relating to groups of inspectional employees should seek to improve the overall pattern ... rather than to attempt to patch the existing uncoordinated pay structure.","explanation":"Both reject expanding special benefits group by group and favor a coordinated government-wide personnel policy."},{"child_excerpt":"although the bill seems to have the sound objective ... I do not believe that it moves toward this objective in a proper manner. A firmer, more acceptable step would be ... Recommendations to the Congress will be made on this matter early in the next session.","parent_excerpt":"even though the problems which the bill seeks to solve are real and pressing. I intend to have these problems further explored ... Upon completion of these studies, I hope to be able to make recommendations to the Congress for necessary legislation.","explanation":"The closing sequence is substantially parallel: concede the real objective, reject the proposed method, identify a broader approach, and promise future recommendations."}]}
